description.narrative: Zimbabwe has laws & policies on VAWG/SGBV/HP that adequately respond to the rights of all women & girls, including exercise/access to SRHR, are evidenced-based & in line with international HR standards & treaties and the Constitution

comment.narrative: Partial alignment of SI related laws( e.g. Marriages , Disability and Child rights laws ) to the Constitution

1. 200 women and girls with disabilities capacitated on and supported to participate in law and policy making processes. 2. National Inquiry on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse of Vulnerable and Marginalized Groups through Child Marriages in Zimbabwe conducted. 3. PSC Gender Equality and Sexual Harassment Module developed and rolled out. 4. Public Service Sexual harassment policy adopted, launched and rolled out. 5. 10 Groups of women and girls trained and supported to start projects under the Women Economic Empowerment. 6. Monitoring and oversight thematic reports on SGBV/SRHR/HP produced by Parliament of Zimbabwe.

1. In 2022, over 1200 women and girls with disabilities in Chipinge, Mt Darwin and Epworth districts were capacitated on the law and policy making processes, SGBV, HP, SRHR and gender equality issues. the capacitated women and girls with disabilities were also supported to participate during the public consultations for a number of bills which include the Labour Amendment Bill, Public Service Bill, the Feedback meeting on the 2022 National Budget, and the 2023 pre budget processes. 2. The Gender Commission with support from UNDP undertook the national inquiry on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse of Vulnerable and marginalised groups such as young women and girls and young people with disabilities through child marriages in Zimbabwe. The inquiry interrogated the efficacy of access to justice and social protection mechanisms especially for young women, girls, and young people with disabilities in the affected communities, and it was evident that most cases of exploitation go unreported or are handled at the family level. A total of 283 survivors of child marriages were interviewed, with 2470 community interactions conducted in all the ten provinces of Zimbabwe. Furthermore, the ZGC received 529 reported cases (10 male and 519 female, and 48 female persons with disabilities) against an annual target of 344 cases. 3.In 2022, UNDP working with the Public Service Commission supported the finalization of the Public Service Sexual Harassment Policy, which was adopted by Cabinet and launched in July 2022. The Policy informed the design of the Public Service Gender and Sexual Harassment module, which is currently undergoing rollout and institutionalization processes. Utilizing the module, the Public Service Academy trained 150 Public Servants Trainers, who will in turn rollout the training to the 13 Training Centres at sub -national levels. 4. The Public Sexual Harassment Policy was approved by Cabinet in April 2022, and launched in July 2022. 5. 14 groups of survivors of SGBV and marginalized women and girls in Chipinge, Mzingwane and Mzarabani were capacitated on business management, financial literacy and skills, record keeping, and drying foods for selling. 5 of the groups received solar dryers under the auspices of the Women Economic Empowerment. 10 beneficiaries from 5 groups were also supported to participate and exhibit at the National Women Economic Empowerment Summit. 6.In 2022, the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Enterprises Development with support from UNDP undertook the development of the Women in Leadership and Decision Making Strategy. The development of the National Strategy was informed by a national consultative process and validations, before it was tabled to the Minister for endorsement. The strategy which is expected to be launched in 2023, and rolled out before the 2023 harmonised elections.

1. Marriages Bill in Parliament Pending Approval 2. Principles for the Sexual Harassment and Gender Equality Bills developed (activity 1.1.10) 3. GBV dedicated Call centers for 3 SI partners developed (activity 2.1.3) 4. Public Service Sexual Harassment Policy developed (activity 2.1.4) 5. High Level Political Compact Launched and Operationalized (activity 2.2.6) 6. Women in decision making strategy developed and launched (activity 3.3.9)

1. Senators who include traditional leaders -chiefs previously trained in SGBV, HPs and SRHRs and marriage bill analysis in 2019 and 2020 cumulatively demonstrated appreciation of the Marriages Bill. Senators eloquently debated the contents of the Bill as evidenced in the Hansards and the local newspapers. The Marriages Bill was was subjected to second reading in the Senate in April 2021 to consider further incorporations of inputs from stakeholders including from CSOs , in particular Womens Groups and the RUNOs participating in SI - clarifying the role of marriage officers including chiefs . However , there were issues on not making lobola or bride price a condition for customary marriage as it was argued that this contradicted international law. The Bill was further discussed in August 2021 in the Senate and traditional leaders and the Minister for Justice engaged on the sticky issue of lobola. There were still on -going negotiations between the executive and senate on to reach a consensus or a compromise. As a result of support to various NGOs by the SI, an NGO called Shamwari Dzevanasikana lodged a Petition to Parliament in September advocating for acceleration of the passing of the Marriages Bill in to law. A key observation has been increased awareness on SI issues amongst Parliamentarians and the public. 2. Principles for the Sexual Harassment Bill and Gender Equality Bill were produced and submitted for approval. the CO supported the Ministry of Women Affairs Community, Small and Medium Enterprises Development and the Gender Commission to engage an expert to lead on the development of the principles through undertaking desk research and consultations with key stakeholders. Three webinar series were conducted to solicit input and views from government stakeholders, the academia, CSOs and labor organizations. the webinars were attended by 110 participants, 59% females and 41% males). after the webinar series, the draft principles were also consulted on in Bulawayo, Mutare, Masvingo, Hwange and Gwanda. after this physical consultations, the draft principles were finalized and validated by the MOWACSMED and the Gender Commission before submission for approval. 3. The CO supported the installation of call centers for three SI partners, the Legal Aid Directorate, the Zimbabwe Republic Police Victim Friendly Unit, and the immigration department. Equipment for the call centers was purchased, installed and we are now at the testing stage. Training workshops on the use of the call centers were convened for the officials from the three partners. Furthermore, Standard Operating Procedures for the call centers were developed and validated. The next step is the launch of the three call centers set for early 2022. 4. A draft of the Public Service Sexual Harassment Policy is in place and set to be launched in 2022. the policy was informed by findings from the baseline study undertaken within the public service on sexual harassment, key informant interviews. lessons learnt from other jurisdiction and the legislative frameworks in the country. several consultative write shops were convened in the process of developing the policy to ensure it speaks to the context and needs with the public service. 5. The HLPC was launched on the 27th of October 2021 by the President of Zimbabwe, EU Ambassador, UN resident coordinator, Minister of women affairs, key government stakeholders, representatives from CSOs, Chapter 12 institutions and traditional leaders. The launch of the compact is a key milestone in Zimbabwe’s journey towards the realization of gender equality and respect for the rights of women and girls meant to ensure that women and girls realize their full potential in a violence-free, gender-responsive and inclusive society. 6. A draft national strategy on women in politics and decision making was developed
1. Disabled Persons sensitized on SI issues 2. SI Targeted Parliament committees sensitized on SI issues

Persons with disabilities in Chipinge, Umzingwane and Harare were sensitized on SI issues so as to empower them to participate effectively in the law making process. Consequently , facilitated by a DPO Leonard Cheshire , Persons with disabilities participated in Public Hearings on Constitutional Amendment No 2 and had their voices heard as acknowledged in the Parliament Committee Report . Furthermore 30 MPs , being members of the Parliament Committee on Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare were sensitized on SI and legal and policy issues resulting in strong commitment to expedite the alignment of disability laws to the Constitution.

description.narrative: Number of inquiries conducted by human rights institutions on VAWG and/or gender equality and non-discrimination in the country within the last 2 years

Number of key informal decision makers and decision makers in relevant institutions with strengthened awareness of and capacities to advocate for the implementation of legislation and policies on VAWG including SGBV/HP and for gender-equitable norms, attitudes and behaviours and women and girls’ rights

Number of women and girls’ survivors/victims and their families, including groups facing multiple and intersecting forms or discrimination, that have increased knowledge of and access to accompaniment/support initiatives, including longer-term recovery services

Number of new and/or strengthened laws and/or policies on ending VAWG and/or gender equality and non-discrimination developed that respond to the rights of women and girls facing intersecting and multiple forms of discrimination and are in line with international human rights standards

Number of targeted national and sub-national training institutions for public servants that have integrated gender equality and ending VAWG, including SGBV/HP and the promotion of women and girls’ SRHR, in their curriculum as per international standards
Number of annual meetings of national and/or sub-national multi-stakeholder coordination mechanisms

Number of institutions that develop strategies, plans and/or programmes to prevent and respond to VAWG, including SGBV/HP, and promote women and girls’ SRHR, including for women and girls facing intersecting and multiple forms of discrimination
